label: copy-phase input u (fed-back u), strongest when next output is 0 or u sits mid-sequence
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, and almost only when the fed-back input is the letter u (97% of activation mass; the rest is a fed-back 0, usually the first of a repeated 0 0 pair). It never fires in the original phase, at the delimiter, or on the first occurrence of a token. But only about 5% of copy-phase u inputs activate it. Activation is stronger when the next output is 0 (the original sequence had u 0; this covers the top examples, e.g. y h u 0 ... -> [u] while outputting 0) and when u is in the middle of a long sequence (recall_idx 3-4, at least 3 outputs left; L=9 holds 51% of mass). Copy-phase u inputs right after the delimiter or near the end rarely fire. Copy-phase u & (output 0 | recall_idx>=3 & to_go>=3) has dev mass recall 0.91 but precision only 0.21, so the full gating condition is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: u, 0, -, b, d, n; least: 3, t, l, <DEL>) and the token being output (most: 0, u, d, y, b, w; least: o, l, -, p); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, L=9 & t=12, L=7 & t=10.
